articles.title: New API Documentation
articles.description: Build with one unified API. Access multiple AI models through a consistent interface.

sections.title: One gateway, multiple providers
sections.body: New API routes client requests to configured channels. Developers use a gateway API key; administrators manage upstream credentials, model names, routing and prices. OpenAI, Anthropic Messages and Gemini entry points are registered, but each model and channel supports a particular set of endpoints.

sections.title: Start with your role
sections.body: Use Quickstart to create a key, choose a model and send a request. Platform administrators should configure a channel, its models, pricing and routing before inviting users. The catalog reflects enabled channel abilities and visible groups; it is not a guarantee that every API key can call every listed model.

articles.title: Quickstart
articles.description: Create a key, choose a model and make your first request.

sections.title: Create an account and API key
sections.body: Open Sign up if registration is enabled, then sign in and open **API Keys**. Create a key with an appropriate group, quota, expiry and model restrictions. Store it in `NEW_API_KEY` on your server. Never use the upstream channel credential or put this key in browser code.

sections.title: Choose a chat model
sections.body: The examples select a model from the API key-scoped `/v1/models` response and check its advertised OpenAI endpoint support. Set `NEW_API_MODEL` to choose a particular accessible chat model, or leave it unset to select the first compatible model. No model name is hard-coded. Catalog visibility and key access can differ.

sections.title: Send a request
sections.body: Set `NEW_API_BASE_URL` to the gateway origin, without `/v1`. Choose a language below. Install `openai` for Python or JavaScript; the cURL example additionally uses `jq`. If no suitable model exists, ask an administrator to configure a chat channel.

sections.title: Check usage and logs
sections.body: Open **Dashboard** for aggregate usage and **Usage Logs → Common Logs** for request records. Check the requested model, group, consumption, errors and latency. Failed or incomplete requests need investigation before retrying.

articles.title: Base URL
articles.description: Use the gateway address for clients and the provider address for channels.

sections.title: Client addresses
sections.body: OpenAI SDKs use the gateway origin followed by `/v1`. Anthropic SDKs use the origin without `/v1`, because the SDK adds `/v1/messages`. Gemini uses the origin with API version `v1beta`. Preserve any deployment path prefix configured by your reverse proxy.

sections.title: Upstream addresses
sections.body: A channel Base URL points to the upstream provider and is configured by an administrator. It is different from the gateway URL used by clients. Use HTTPS for public deployments; keep credentials out of URLs.

articles.title: Authentication
articles.description: Relay API keys, management access tokens and browser sessions have different purposes.

sections.title: Relay requests
sections.body: Send a key created in **API Keys** as `Authorization: Bearer <NEW_API_KEY>`. Anthropic Messages also accepts `x-api-key`; Gemini paths accept `x-goog-api-key`. Prefer headers to query-string credentials. Key status, expiry, quota, model restrictions, IP restrictions and group access are enforced by the server.

sections.title: Console and management
sections.body: The console uses a short-lived access JWT in memory and a rotating HttpOnly refresh cookie backed by server sessions. A personal management access token is separate from a relay API key. Administrator and root routes apply their own authorization and may require permission checks or security verification. Do not substitute a relay key for an administrator credential.

sections.title: Credential hygiene
sections.body: Keep credentials in server environment variables or a secret manager. Rotate a compromised key and revoke affected sessions from Security. Never include passwords, verification codes, refresh cookies or usable tokens in troubleshooting screenshots or logs.

articles.title: FAQ
articles.description: Resolve common setup and compatibility questions.

sections.title: Why is a catalog model rejected?
sections.body: The catalog lists visible groups and configured channel abilities. Your key can have a different group, model allowlist, expiry or quota. Check `/v1/models` with that key, then confirm that the chosen endpoint is supported.

sections.title: Why does the copied price differ from a log?
sections.body: A displayed base price can be modified by group ratios, cache categories, expression tiers, request conditions or provider-specific task usage. The consumption log records settlement. The pre-consumed reservation is not always the final charge.

sections.title: Does a compatible endpoint support every upstream feature?
sections.body: No. Conversion and provider behavior depend on the selected channel. Unsupported fields, modes and tools may be rejected. File storage and fine-tuning routes registered as unimplemented are excluded from the supported API reference.

articles.title: OpenAI
articles.description: Configure the SDK against the actual gateway protocol.

sections.title: Install and configure
sections.body: Use `pip install openai` / `npm install openai` for OpenAI, `pip install anthropic` / `npm install @anthropic-ai/sdk` for Anthropic, or `pip install google-genai` / `npm install @google/genai` for Gemini. Set the gateway origin, API key and an accessible model advertising the selected protocol. cURL uses the same headers and request body without an SDK.

sections.title: Minimal request and streaming
sections.body: The example uses a model selected by you and checked against the credential-scoped model list. Enable streaming only if the selected upstream supports it. Anthropic produces message events, Gemini streams GenerateContent responses, and OpenAI Chat produces chat completion chunks. These envelopes are not interchangeable.

sections.title: Errors and multimodal input
sections.body: Check the HTTP status and structured error before retrying. Start with a text request. Add images, audio or tools only when the model metadata and upstream documentation support them; the existence of a gateway route does not prove model capability.

articles.title: Model Catalog
articles.description: Live models, endpoint compatibility and prices from the existing catalog.

sections.title: Catalog source
sections.body: This catalog shares `/api/pricing` and the pricing page query cache. The backend builds it from enabled channel abilities, model metadata, vendors, endpoint support and effective pricing. Visibility follows the configured pricing module and usable groups.

sections.title: Access and missing metadata
sections.body: A listed model may be inaccessible to a particular key. Use `/v1/models` with that key to verify access. Unspecified context, modalities or capabilities are shown as unknown; no model-name heuristic is used. Coming soon and deprecated states are not invented.

articles.title: Compatibility Matrix
articles.description: Compare only endpoint types and capabilities reported by the backend.

sections.title: Read the matrix
sections.body: Supported APIs come from `supported_endpoint_types` and the server endpoint map. These are configured protocol bindings, not a promise of complete feature parity. Capabilities and modalities appear only when supplied by catalog metadata.

sections.title: Before choosing a model
sections.body: Check the endpoint, then confirm the model is in your key-scoped list. For streaming, tools, reasoning or structured output, test the selected channel with a small request. Blank metadata means unknown rather than unsupported.

articles.title: Pricing
articles.description: Use configured prices and the same display logic as Model Square.

sections.title: Effective prices
sections.body: The table uses the existing ModelPriceCell, including token prices, per-request prices, expression-based tiers, cache categories and provider variants. Without a selected group it follows Model Square and displays the lowest enabled group multiplier. Choose a group to view its multiplier and matching models. The catalog is read-only.

sections.title: Task and provider variants
sections.body: Task schemas identify canonical billing units such as seconds, counts, tokens and credits. Different plugins serving the same model can use different schemas and expressions. Unconfigured provider pricing must be corrected by an administrator before submission.

sections.title: Platform price and upstream cost
sections.body: Platform consumption is controlled by New API pricing. An upstream provider cost is a separate value; do not assume that a catalog price is the provider invoice or that every provider publishes cost data.

articles.title: Billing
articles.description: Understand reservations, actual usage, settlement and refunds.

sections.title: Request lifecycle
sections.body: The request path resolves effective pricing and group access, estimates usage, reserves quota when required, executes the provider, then settles measured or locally estimated usage. The billing session reconciles the reservation with the final charge. Failure refund policy runs after eligible attempts end; a settled session is not refunded twice.

sections.title: Token and request pricing
sections.body: Text expressions use USD per million tokens. Input, output, cache, image and audio token categories are separated only when the expression explicitly prices them. Context tier conditions use total input length, not the input remainder after cache subtraction. Fixed request leaves charge per successful request, not per streamed chunk. Legacy ratio and per-call pricing remain supported.

sections.title: Image, video and audio quantities
sections.body: Images can use image count, tokens or a task schema. Video tasks can use seconds, counts, vendor credits or tokens. Audio pricing depends on the actual relay or task implementation; there is no universal duration or character rule. Read the live schema and expression for the chosen model instead of inferring a unit from its modality.

sections.title: Asynchronous settlement
sections.body: Task submission freezes its selected expression and usage facts. Completion overlays validated measured facts and reconciles quota. Missing completion facts retain submission values; evaluation failure retains the reservation and records a warning. The task record and consumption log are the sources for settlement troubleshooting.

sections.title: Wallet and subscriptions
sections.body: Funding can come from a wallet or a subscription under the configured billing preference. Subscription reservations and asynchronous tasks do not use the wallet trust bypass. Group changes on retry refresh group-dependent reservation values before another provider attempt.

articles.description: Registered API surface with model-specific compatibility limits.

sections.title: Endpoint

`/v1/chat/completions`

Use `model` and `messages`. Streaming uses OpenAI-style SSE chunks. Tools and response formats are conditional on the selected provider.

sections.title: Request and response contract
sections.body: Use API Reference for registered methods, middleware and matched OpenAPI schemas. An OpenAPI schema is a checked-in contract, not a recorded upstream response. Where no current schema exists, the reference identifies that gap instead of inventing fields.

sections.title: Choose a compatible model
sections.body: Open the live catalog and check Supported APIs. Verify the model with your API key before calling. For multipart and asynchronous operations, follow the operation-specific schema and inspect the HTTP response before attempting to parse it.

articles.title: Claude Code
articles.description: Connect a client using supported gateway protocols.

sections.title: Configuration
sections.body: Select an Anthropic-compatible model and configure `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to the gateway origin, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` to your gateway key and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to the accessible model ID. The Messages route exists, but `/v1/messages/count_tokens` is disabled in this repository. Client features requiring that route or provider-specific beta features may fail.

sections.title: Verify the connection
sections.body: Create a dedicated gateway key for this client, verify model access, send a small request, then inspect Usage Logs. If authentication succeeds but generation fails, check the endpoint type and channel health. This guide describes protocol configuration; it is not a certification of every client version.

sections.body: Consult the [official client documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway) for the current settings UI.

articles.title: Streaming
articles.description: Practical guidance constrained by the actual protocol and provider.

sections.title: Workflow
sections.body: Use `stream: true` only with a supported model and endpoint. OpenAI Chat streams SSE chunks, Anthropic streams message events, and Gemini uses its own stream shape. Keep proxy buffering disabled and timeouts long enough for generation. Do not concatenate arbitrary event JSON as final text.

sections.title: Validate with your deployment
sections.body: Use the catalog to inspect endpoint support, make a minimal request, and check Usage Logs. Add one feature at a time. Consult API Reference and the selected upstream contract when field support differs.

articles.title: Tool Calling
articles.description: Practical guidance constrained by the actual protocol and provider.

sections.title: Workflow
sections.body: Pass protocol-specific tool definitions only to a provider that supports them. A tool call is a request for your application to execute a function; the gateway does not execute your local function. Validate arguments and permissions, run the tool, and return the result using the same conversation protocol.

articles.title: Retry & Error Handling
articles.description: Practical guidance constrained by the actual protocol and provider.

sections.title: Workflow
sections.body: Inspect HTTP status and structured errors. Correct authentication, access and request validation failures before retrying. For rate limiting or transient upstream failure, use bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter. Do not automatically resubmit an ambiguous asynchronous creation: it can duplicate billable work. Streams may report an error after HTTP headers were sent.

articles.title: Overview
articles.description: Use the current console menu and workflow.

sections.title: Where to find it
sections.body:
Open **Overview** at `/dashboard`.

Use Dashboard for an overview of consumption and request activity. Model Call Analytics and Flow are separate sections. User Analytics is restricted to administrators.

sections.title: Restrictions and troubleshooting
sections.body: The server checks your role, group and permissions. Some controls appear only when enabled by platform settings. If a request is rejected, check the visible error and your account status; do not use administrator routes to work around an access restriction.

sections.title: Where to find it

articles.title: Administration
articles.description: Operate the platform through its existing administrator tools.

sections.title: Workflow
sections.body: Platform operations are separate from developer API access. Begin with a channel and valid upstream credentials, configure model names and groups, test the channel, then set pricing and routing. Admin/root permissions and delegated resource permissions govern each operation.

sections.title: Verify before enabling traffic
sections.body: Save the intended configuration, test a supported request and inspect the relevant logs. Confirm group access, pricing and channel selection together. A channel test is not a certification of every model, modality or endpoint.

articles.title: API Reference
articles.description: Generated route inventory joined to matching checked-in OpenAPI schemas.

sections.title: Source and coverage
sections.body: Methods and paths are extracted from Go router syntax and the host protocol registry. Only matching OpenAPI operations contribute schemas. Routes registered as unimplemented and stale OpenAPI paths are excluded. Native plugin routes depend on installed plugins and are outside this static route inventory.

sections.title: Authentication and schemas
sections.body: Each operation shows its declared middleware. Relay uses API keys; management routes may require user, administrator, root, resource permissions or security verification. Parameters, request and response schemas are shown when a matching checked-in OpenAPI operation exists. Examples and actual responses are not fabricated.

articles.title: Request Headers
articles.description: Use protocol-specific headers without confusing client keys with channel credentials.

sections.title: Headers
sections.body: Send `Authorization: Bearer <NEW_API_KEY>` for relay calls and `Content-Type: application/json` for JSON requests. Anthropic also uses `x-api-key` and its protocol version header. Gemini accepts `x-goog-api-key`. Multipart clients should let the HTTP library generate the boundary.

sections.title: Forwarded and administrative headers
sections.body: Channel configuration controls upstream header overrides. Do not send provider credentials from a browser or assume arbitrary headers bypass server authorization. Request conditions can influence configured pricing, so consult Billing for the model rather than treating beta headers as universally free.

articles.title: Error Codes
articles.description: Generated gateway error constants with no invented status mapping.

sections.title: Interpret errors
sections.body: The index below is generated from ErrorCode declarations. HTTP status depends on the call site, adaptor and upstream response; there is no universal constant-to-status map. Inspect both status and `error.code` / protocol-specific error fields.

sections.title: Suggested action
sections.body: For request errors, correct the request shape and endpoint. For access errors, check key restrictions and account status. For pricing or channel errors, ask the administrator to review configuration. For upstream errors, inspect the provider response and avoid unbounded retries.

articles.title: Rate Limits
articles.description: Limits depend on deployment settings and user group.

sections.title: Configured limits
sections.body: Model request limits can track total attempts and successful requests within configured windows. Group-specific limits can override global model limits. API, login and email paths also have their own protection. No fixed public RPM/TPM value is implied by the gateway.

sections.title: When limited
sections.body: Check the actual HTTP response, wait before retrying and use bounded backoff. Some limit paths return a status without a JSON body; do not assume every 429 contains an OpenAI error object. Administrators manage these controls under Security → Rate Limiting.

articles.title: Payment Webhooks
articles.description: Inbound payment callbacks are distinct from asynchronous AI task polling.

sections.title: Payment callbacks
sections.body: The gateway registers provider-specific payment callback routes, including Stripe, Creem and configured Waffo integrations. Configure the matching payment provider with the deployment URL and its required verification settings. These routes are not a generic task completion callback service.

sections.title: Task completion
sections.body: AI task completion is handled by polling and protocol retrieval unless a particular installed plugin explicitly provides a native mechanism. Do not expect a generic outbound webhook from the presence of payment webhook routes.
